newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks down 3.27 pct in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks down 3.27 pct in late trade.

text.p: Jakarta stocks plunged in late trading on Friday on rupiah worries as the currency further weakened against the dollar, brokers said.
The composite index fell 21.03 points, or 3.27 percent, to 621.98 points at 0805 GMT. Decliners led gainers by 122 to seven with 27 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 311 billion rupiah.
"The market turned panicky after the rupiah fell to 2,900 (against the dollar). Players, both local and foreign, were in a selling spree after the fall," one broker said.
Analysts said the stock market has become the victim of the turmoil in the currency markets and its trend in the near term would largely depend on what happened to the rupiah.

"The stock market has become the victim of the currency markets. How long would the market remain like this ? It will largely depend on the currency markets," Goei Siauw Hong, an analyst with Socgen Crosby Securities, said.
The rupiah fell to a new record low of 2,960 to the dollar in the afternoon from its opening level of 2,770/90, leading to panic selling by local and foreign investors, brokers said.
Among individual stocks, Bank International Indonesia (BII) topped the active list, with 51 million shares traded. It fell 200 rupiah to close at a year-low of 1,200 rupiah.

Analysts said BII' falls were due to worries that the bank which derive large parts of its net income from the foreign exchange market and trade financing would be hit by the volatile currency markets.

The largest state-owned bank, Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI), closed 150 rupiah lower at 1,200 rupiah after touching a year-low of 1,175 rupiah as the bank also derives large parts of its earnings from the foreign exchange market, analysts said.
